_readme: The repo list is fetched automatically from GitHub (see the GITHUB_ORG env var / prompt). Only add an entry to this file when a project needs a special setting that differs from the generic (auto-detected) behavior. Key = must exactly match the GitHub repo name. If secretManager is '1password', op://vault/item/field references are filled in with real values via 'op inject' (the 1Password CLI must be installed and signed in); otherwise, if nothing is configured, the tool interactively asks how to fill in .env (1Password / copy from a local checkout / skip) every run -- see README.md's Secret Management section for both the static (this file) and dynamic (interactive) paths, and scripts/migrate-env-to-1password.js for pre-populating a 1Password item to use with the static path. By default the op:// references are read from the project's own .env.example -- but that means committing your vault/item layout into the shared team repo. Prefer envTemplateFile instead: a path (relative to THIS tool's repo root, e.g. 'config/env-templates/<repo>.env.tpl') to a template that lives only here, never in the cloned repo. If healthCheckPort is given, after 'docker compose up' the tool waits until that port starts listening; if not given, the first published port in docker-compose.yml is auto-detected. For projects that don't require Docker, if runCommand is given (e.g. 'npm run start:dev') that command is run in the background after setup; if not given, the dev/start/serve script in package.json is used, then for Laravel projects (if an artisan file exists) 'php artisan serve', and if none of those apply, a safe command (starting with npm/yarn/pnpm) found in README.md. If runPort is given, that port is health-checked directly instead of guessing it from logs. In postCloneCommands auto-detection, 'composer install' is also added if composer.json exists (it can coexist with npm/yarn/pnpm in the same repo).
